title: Corporate yacht catering in Dubai: food for a business charter
body_html:
Corporate yacht catering is a business meeting that happens to be on the water: the agenda, the guest mix and the boat's own constraints all shape what food works. This guide covers the formats that suit a working charter, how service timing follows the itinerary, and what to confirm before boarding. One thing it does not cover is the vessel itself — myCHEF provides the food, chef and service only, never the boat. The yacht catering in Dubai page lists the onboard formats available.

What changes when the meeting is on a yacht

  • Galley and deck space are fixed and small, so formats that need little last-minute work — canapés, boxed lunches, one-pot mains — travel better than elaborate plated menus.
  • Guests cannot leave, so service must fit between agenda blocks; there is no foyer to escape to.
  • Swimming or sightseeing stops pause service; agree in advance whether food waits or the window moves.
  • Dietary notes matter more at sea: there is no corner shop. Collect them with the RSVP, not at boarding.

Corporate yacht catering formats by agenda

Charter purposeFormatService note
Client hospitality or networkingPassed canapés plus a drinks stationFlow service across the cruise; no fixed sit-down
Team offsite with a working sessionBoxed lunches labelled by dietary needHand out at the agenda's lunch block; minimal table space needed
Board or investor dinnerSeated dinner on the aft deckNeeds the calm-water stretch; schedule around it
All-day charterLight brunch, afternoon grill, sunset bitesThree windows tied to the itinerary, not the clock

A worked example (hypothetical)

Sixteen guests, a four-hour afternoon charter with a one-hour working session aboard. Boarding at 15:00 with welcome drinks and canapés; the working session runs 16:00 to 17:00 with no service; a boxed lunch with dietary labels is distributed at 17:05 as the boat anchors; light dessert and coffee from 18:00 during the return leg. Arrival, anchoring and return times come from the charter operator — the caterer plans against those times, so share them before the day.

What to confirm before boarding

  • The itinerary's fixed times: departure, anchoring, return — service is planned against them.
  • Vessel rules on food and drinks, and what the operator supplies versus what arrives with the caterer.
  • Where the crew prefers service to happen: aft deck, salon or a mix.
  • A wet-weather or swell fallback: which format still works if the deck is off-limits.

Next steps

Send the charter times, guest count, agenda blocks and dietary notes through the yacht catering page and ask for a service plan timed to the itinerary. Related guides: connecting a chef to your charter and a three-hour yacht food timeline.
